events.title: A Traveling Minstrel
events.text: A dusty minstrel plays three songs for his supper. The room hums along and forgets its grudges.

events.title: The Tavern Cat
events.text: A ginger cat strolls in, inspects the hearth, and claims the warmest stool as though it holds the deed. The guests approve.

events.title: A Spilled Cask
events.text: A cask slips its chock in the cellar and glugs itself empty across the stones. The smell is wonderful. The loss is not.

events.title: A Merchant's Gratitude
events.text: A merchant whose axle you let mend in the yard last month settles his old tab — with interest.

events.title: The Duke's Assessor
events.text: A thin man with a thick ledger counts your chimneys, mutters 'two', and presents a levy on the spot.

events.title: A Bargain on Barrels
events.text: A carter undersold on the pass road offers a barrel of mead below cost, no questions welcome.

events.title: An Old Feud Flares
events.text: Two families who stopped speaking a generation ago pick tables in earshot of each other. The air goes taut as a bowstring.

events.title: Dwarven Song Night
events.text: Every dwarf in the room finds the same low harmony at the same moment. Stone songs make the walls feel thicker and the night safer.

events.title: A Goblin Dice Ring
events.text: Someone's running weighted dice under the corner table. By the time you notice, three purses are lighter and one temper is not.

events.title: A Sudden Storm
events.text: Rain hits the shutters like flung gravel. Everyone within a mile of the Flagon suddenly remembers how much they love a warm hearth.

events.title: A Cold Snap
events.text: Frost in the small hours. The hearth gulps wood, the kitchen runs slow, and the stew pot never quite comes back to a boil.

events.title: Long Midsummer Light
events.text: The evening light refuses to leave, gilding every mug on the counter. Guests linger, and lingering guests order twice.

events.title: Aldous's Little Cache
events.text: A floorboard by the hearth gives underfoot. Beneath it: a tin of coins and a note in a familiar hand — 'For the night you think you can't. You can.'

events.title: The White Stag
events.text: A white stag stands in the yard for a full minute, breath steaming, watching the door. The old folk say it only visits houses the forest trusts.

events.title: A Tremor in the Stones
events.text: For one heartbeat every candle leans the same way and the cellar stones hum like a struck bell. Whatever sleeps below the Flagon is not sleeping well.
